title: The Amount Claimed for a Surrendered Journey — Travel Protection Plans
content:
A traveller who has given up an insured journey files one claim against the cancellation benefit of their Travel Protection Plans certificate for the prepaid outlay they cannot get back.

**The amount claimed.** It is the declared trip cost the certificate carries, less the value the operator has given back and less the share of the deposit the operator returns, taken at the share promptness carries, and rounded to two decimal places; it never falls below nothing.

**The value the operator has given back.** None of it is taken off.

**The share of the deposit the operator returns.** It is half of it, 50 per cent.

**The share promptness carries.** It is 75 per cent.

## The quantity defined in order

The declared trip cost the certificate carries is the starting figure. From it are subtracted the value the operator has given back and the share of the deposit the operator returns, that share being taken of the deposit paid on the linked package. The figure that results is floored at nothing before anything else is done to it. It is then taken at the share promptness carries, and the result is rounded to two decimal places. The share promptness carries acts on the figure after the two subtractions, not on the declared trip cost itself.

## Worked to a figure on hypothetical inputs

Take a certificate declaring a trip cost of 7000.00 USD, on a linked package against which a deposit of 1000.00 USD was paid.

- The declared trip cost the certificate carries is 7000.00 USD.
- None of the value the operator has given back is taken off, so 0.00 USD comes off on that account.
- The share of the deposit the operator returns is 50 per cent of the 1000.00 USD deposit, which is 500.00 USD, and that comes off.
- The figure after the two subtractions is 6500.00 USD, which is above nothing.
- Taken at the share promptness carries, 75 per cent, that is 4875.00 USD.

The amount claimed, rounded to two decimal places, is 4875.00 USD.

Where the two subtractions would carry the figure below nothing — on a declared trip cost of 400.00 USD against a deposit share of 500.00 USD, for instance — the figure is nothing, and the amount claimed is 0.00 USD.
